prompt: Two rivers rendered as abstract watercolor washes, painted in perspective as if the viewer stands at the point where the rivers meet. The left river recedes from lower-center toward the upper-left, its painted form narrowing with distance, a cool blue-gray wash with soft feathered edges and thin ink lines tracing its channel. The right river recedes from lower-center toward the upper-right, painted in warm slate-gray, also narrowing into the distance. At the bottom-center of the composition the two river forms are widest and closest, nearly touching — the meeting point. Bare cream parchment surrounds the forms.

A perspective watercolor of two abstract river channels approaching the viewer. One river flows from the upper-left distance toward the lower-center foreground, its wash of cool slate-blue widening as it comes forward. The other flows from the upper-right distance toward the same lower-center point, painted in warm gray-brown, also widening toward the viewer. The two rivers meet and blend in a soft confluence at the bottom-center of the image, which is the closest point to the viewer. Delicate ink lines follow each channel. Cream parchment is mostly bare around the forms.

Two watercolor river shapes painted in one-point perspective, each receding from a shared foreground meeting point. The left river starts wide at the lower-center, its blue-gray wash tapering as it winds away toward the upper-left corner. The right river starts equally wide at the same foreground point, its teal-gray wash tapering as it curves away toward the upper-right. The convergence zone — where the two rivers are at their widest and most vivid — sits near the bottom center, pulling the viewer's eye in. Thin pencil-fine ink lines sketch the river bends. Generous bare parchment all around.

An abstract watercolor illustration of two rivers meeting the viewer. From the lower-center foreground — the confluence point — one river sweeps away toward the upper-left in a receding arc of cool indigo-blue wash, narrowing with perspective. The other river sweeps away toward the upper-right in a warm gray wash, also narrowing into the distance. The foreground where they join is wide, vivid, and lush with layered pigment and blooming edges. Further from the viewer the washes thin to whisper-fine strokes. Ink lines trace the channel edges throughout. Cream parchment all around.

Two rivers painted as loose watercolor washes flowing toward the viewer in perspective, meeting at the closest point at the bottom-center of the composition. The right river curves in from the upper-right background — a narrow teal ribbon that grows wider, richer, and more layered as it approaches — until it meets the left river at the foreground. The left river mirrors this, a cool blue-gray wash narrowing into the upper-left distance. At their meeting point the colors merge in a soft bloom. Spare ink lines define the banks. Bare parchment fills the rest of the image.

A minimalist watercolor study showing two rivers in perspective, converging toward the viewer. Each river is painted as an abstract wash — one in cool dusty blue, one in warm gray-brown — that begins as a thin receding line in the upper portion of the image and swells progressively wider as it flows forward toward the lower-center meeting point. The confluence is the widest, boldest part of the painting, with soft blooming pigment and layered washes suggesting depth and movement. Thin ink lines trace each channel.
